title: Petra and the Postcard
premise: Orsen Pemberton is three missed payments from losing his seaside café when a snowstorm strands Petra Vance — the woman he loved and lost a decade ago — and her estranged business rival, Julian Marsh, in his empty dining room. The two rivals are racing to prove who owns a disputed patent that could save one of their companies and ruin the other, and Orsen, once the anonymous witness whose testimony was buried in their original falling-out, holds the postcard that could settle it. As the storm traps them together, old memories resurface, forcing each to decide whether justice means winning or telling the truth. In the end, Petra chooses honesty over victory, Julian withdraws his claim, and Orsen lets Petra stay past the last train — choosing love over the safe, scheduled life he'd been hiding inside.
about_author: Ivo Sterling is the pen name of a former line cook who spent eleven years working harbor-town cafés before turning to fiction full-time. They write romances about people whose lives are held together by recipes, timetables, and things left unsaid.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen counts down his café's final days while perfecting a cardamom bun recipe his late mother left unfinished. A bank letter arrives; he burns it rather than read it aloud. Emotional beat: quiet dread disguised as routine, establishing his habit of postponing hard truths.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra arrives in the harbor town on the season's final ferry, carrying a legal folder and an old postcard she can't bring herself to throw away. She checks into the inn, planning to confront Julian Marsh at dawn. Emotional beat: resolve layered over homesickness for a life she chose to leave.

chapters.title: Snow Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian drives into town overnight to intercept Petra, confident the patent dispute will end in a signature. The forecast turns; roads close behind him. Emotional beat: control fraying at the edges as weather makes him, for once, powerless.

chapters.title: Stranded at Pemberton's
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The only lit building on the closed main street is Orsen's café. Petra and Julian, mid-argument, take shelter there — and Orsen recognizes Petra instantly, though she doesn't recognize him. Emotional beat: shock masked by professional hospitality.

chapters.title: Cardamom and Cold Coffee
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Over coffee neither rival drinks, Petra and Julian rehash the decade-old dispute that made them enemies. Orsen listens too closely, because he was there. Emotional beat: nostalgia curdling into accusation, with Orsen caught between past and present.

chapters.title: The Postcard He Kept
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Alone in the kitchen, Orsen takes out the postcard Petra sent him ten years ago — unsigned, half-burned, the reason his testimony never reached the lawyers. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing like a bruise; memory theme established fully.

chapters.title: What the Storm Cuts Off
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Phone dead, roads buried, Julian tries to negotiate a private settlement with Petra. She refuses: she wants justice, not a deal. Emotional beat: pride as armor; both rivals reveal they're fighting for someone who isn't themselves.

chapters.title: Flour on Her Sleeves
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Bored and thawing, Petra wanders into the kitchen and Orsen teaches her to fold dough. Muscle memory from their shared past surfaces in her hands before her mind catches up. Emotional beat: tenderness arriving sideways, through craft instead of words.

chapters.title: The Witness Nobody Called
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian mentions the case's missing witness — the barista who saw the original prototype night and then vanished. Orsen says nothing, but his hands shake. Emotional beat: dramatic irony tightening; the reader knows what Julian doesn't.

chapters.title: Candles at Closing Time
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Power fails; the three share candlelight and Orsen's improvised dinner. Petra tells a story about 'someone I knew' — clearly Orsen — while looking at him. Emotional beat: recognition dawning slowly, desire complicated by deception.

chapters.title: She Remembers the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Petra finds the old photo taped inside the register — herself, younger, laughing in this same kitchen. She confronts Orsen: you knew all along. Emotional beat: betrayal and relief colliding; identity theme crystallizes.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Timing
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Orsen explains why he disappeared after the prototype night: he was paid to stay silent, took the money to buy the café, and has regretted it every day since. Emotional beat: confession as catharsis; justice outside the law takes shape.

chapters.title: Julian's Ledger
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian admits he knows more about the missing witness than he let on — he traced Orsen years ago and chose not to use him, out of a shame he's never named. Emotional beat: the rival revealed as a man avoiding his own verdict.

chapters.title: A Verdict Without a Courtroom
chapters.summary: All three, alternating short sections. Around the candlelit table they stage their own trial: testimony, cross-examination, no lawyers. The truth of the prototype night finally gets spoken aloud. Emotional beat: catharsis through informal justice; the novel's thematic core.

chapters.title: The Morning After the Truth
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Snowplows are heard in the distance; rescue is coming, and with it, the world where the trial never happened. Petra must decide what to file with the patent office. Emotional beat: the fragile peace of honesty tested by consequence.

chapters.title: Last Train, First Choice
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The plowed road means Petra can catch the last train to the city and win her case cleanly. Orsen, terrified, asks her to stay until the ferry returns — not forever, just past the deadline. Emotional beat: vulnerability as courage; the blurb's promise delivered.

chapters.title: Withdrawal
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian files to withdraw his patent claim, ending the rivalry on his own terms rather than a court's. He leaves town without goodbye, leaving a note: 'Some debts you pay by walking away.' Emotional beat: grace from an unexpected quarter.

chapters.title: The Bank Letter, Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra finds the unopened bank letter and reads it to Orsen: final notice. Instead of pity, she proposes a partnership — her settlement money, his kitchen, one honest menu. Emotional beat: love expressed as practical faith, not grand gesture.

chapters.title: Reopening Day
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The café reopens with a new sign and the finished cardamom bun recipe, completed with Petra's hands. First customers trickle in; the town watches. Emotional beat: earned joy, small and specific rather than triumphant.

chapters.title: The Ferry Returns
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The first ferry of the new season arrives, symbolically reversing the opening image. Petra stands at the dock and deliberately doesn't board. Emotional beat: choice made visible; identity reclaimed as someone who stays.

chapters.title: Postscript, Unsigned No More
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen writes a postcard of his own — signed, addressed to Petra, slipped under her door though she's twenty feet away. It reads simply: 'Stay.' Emotional beat: the shy gesture completing the arc begun with the burned postcard.

chapters.title: Petra and the Postcard
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, closing. Petra pins both postcards — hers half-burned, his whole — above the café register. Final image: morning light, rising dough, two people who stopped running. Emotional beat: resolution as quiet permanence; memory honored, justice served, identity chosen.
